title: AI is good for everyone, we swear! Trust us!
excerpt: A new wave of ads from Meta and Anthropic puts AI companies on the defensive. Can they win back trust?
content_html:
By Henry Chandonnet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Read in app

Meta's new ad is a Lisa Frank wet dream. There are rainbows, butterflies, bear hugs, and smash-cuts between three grinning children.

It's a smiley, cloying vision for AI. The ad's narrator beckons us to call Meta's staff "optimists" and "dreamers," and says that the company is "betting on people" — tell that to the 8,000 workers Meta just laid off. It promises that the "future is for everyone" — a surprisingly collectivist mission for a company that has recently hired several acolytes of Donald Trump.

While Meta turns up the cheer on AI, the American public has soured. 40% of Americans predict that AI will have a negative impact on society, according to Pew Research Center; only 16% said it would be positive. Nearly three-quarters of Americans are opposed to data centers being built in their area, per Gallup. Protests abound, on TikTok, at City Halls, and outside Anthropic's headquarters.

Meta clearly has something to prove — as do all the AI labs. As executives at Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and beyond change their tone from "AI could wipe out white-collar work" to "AI will be an immaculate boon for humanity," the industry's power players have gone on the defensive.

AI is great, they say. We're leading it with joy and conscientiousness, they say. Trust us, they say.

AI is a unique marketing challenge. A few years ago, it was described as all-powerful — the technological shift to end all technological shifts. It was "even bigger" than a technological revolution, Sam Altman said four months after ChatGPT's launch. Dario Amodei analogized LLMs to a "country of geniuses in a datacenter."

Then there was the productivity wave, promising workers that it would make their jobs so much easier. If you believe Elon Musk, you might not need to work at all. And then there's always China, the looming threat the labs can cite to justify their breakneck speed.

The China warnings aren't going away anytime soon. For all the giddiness of the Meta ad, Sean Spicer reacted with a dour warning. "The US can't lose the AI race to China," the former White House press secretary and onetime "Dancing With The Stars" contestant wrote in a quote tweet of the ad. I emailed Spicer to ask for his thoughts on the ad and what he thought it said about public opinion. He ignored the question. "There is no second place in the race to dominate AI," he wrote.

That's what the AI race has long been about: domination. The labs have tried to dominate in pricing, in talent, in subtle digs on the podcast circuit. Can they soften their image to regain trust?

Anthropic tried with its own barnburner of an ad that it debuted during the World Cup two weeks ago. It showed some terrifying images — facial recognition tracking, a cemetery, and yes, a burning house — while posing some terrifying questions. "Can AI be trusted?" a voiceover asked. "Who's gonna hit the brakes if we need to?" The answer: Anthropic! We here for you.

If the ads prove anything, it's that the AI labs realize how deep the worries have gone.

The ad was widely skewered. Andreessen Horowitz partner Olivia Moore wondered if Anthropic was "actively trying to churn users." Sam Altman wrote that he thought it was satire. And yet, its structure was remarkably similar to the Meta ad in one way: teeing up the criticism, then shutting it down.

Anthropic gives its critics a pat on the head. "If we all had a voice in it, then I feel like it would be better," one voice in the ad says, implying that the public has a voice in Anthropic's development. They don't; it's not even a public company yet. The startup's message that there's "hope in hard questions" doesn't offer any plans for answering them.

Meta, on the other hand, gives its critics the business. "Some people will have you believe AI will make us less connected," the ad's narrator says. "Have you believe" — what is this, hypnosis? Of course, Meta is the savior against these faceless snake-charmers. They're the optimists, the shining knights of the AI race.

It's not just the LLM giants. Notion played into the criticism in its latest campaign: "AI dread" billboards. The software company set up a hotline for callers with a "nagging worry that AI can do our jobs."

Trust is hard to earn. It's not clear that either strategy — the head-pat, the retort — will bring AI's detractors any peace.

Some commenters loved the Meta ad, calling it a solve for growing doomerism. Others called called it "distasteful" and "unbelievably out of touch." Many mocked the score choice: David Bowie's "Five Years," a song about the demise of planet Earth.

David Reibstein, a professor of marketing at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, said that the AI labs had to address growing criticism. Anthropic's ad was "gutsy," he said, while he was less inspired by Meta's. The message is "trust us because we're Facebook," he said. On the criticism that Anthropic raised potential harms that the company itself was abetting those potential harms, he said, "I don't think it's being hypocritical. I think it's being sensitive."

When reached for comment, a Meta representative sent contact information for some advertising executives it said the company had no financial ties to. One of these was Zach Blume, president of the creative agency Portal A, who said he found both ads "powerful and persuasive."

I also asked Joonas Virtanen, a founding designer at the mini-app startup Wabi who had previously helped make Airbnb's chatbots "more fun," what he made of the campaigns. He said that he was more likely to believe Anthropic's approach, calling it an "honest" ad that "treats people like adults." As for Meta, he spat out the sugary sweetness. "It's a little bit of corporate bullshit," he said. "It is selling that rosy vision."

Virtanen works in tech; he's predisposed to AI's benefits. The companies will need to bring in those outside the bubble, those who would rather live near a nuclear reactor than a data center. They'll be harder to convince.

Sure, Amodei has tapered down his warnings of the oncoming AI apocalypse. And sure, Altman said he'd be "delighted to be wrong" about AI job destruction. But the seed is already planted. If the ads prove anything, it's that the AI labs realize how deep the worries have gone. They'll need more than rainbows and "hard questions" to uproot it.

Henry Chandonnet is a reporter on the Business News desk. He mainly writes about AI and tech culture.

作者：Henry Chandonnet 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Meta 的新广告是 Lisa Frank 的梦遗。 影片中有彩虹、蝴蝶、​​熊抱，以及三个咧着嘴笑的孩子之间的精彩剪辑。

这是人工智能的一个微笑的、令人厌烦的愿景。 广告的旁白让我们称 Meta 的员工为“乐观主义者”和“梦想家”，并表示该公司正在“把赌注押在人身上”——告诉 Meta 刚刚解雇的 8,000 名员工。 它承诺“未来属于每个人”——对于一家最近聘请了唐纳德·特朗普的几名助手的公司来说，这是一个令人惊讶的集体主义使命。

尽管 Meta 为人工智能欢呼雀跃，但美国公众却感到不满。 根据皮尤研究中心的数据，40% 的美国人预测人工智能将对社会产生负面影响；只有 16% 的人表示这是积极的。 根据盖洛普的数据，近四分之三的美国人反对在他们所在地区建立数据中心。 在 TikTok 上、市政厅以及 Anthropic 总部外，抗议活动比比皆是。

Meta 显然有一些东西需要证明——就像所有的人工智能实验室一样。 随着 Anthropic、OpenAI、SpaceXAI 等公司的高管将口吻从“人工智能可能消灭白领工作”转变为“人工智能将为人类带来完美的福祉”，该行业的巨头们已经采取了守势。

他们说，人工智能很棒。 他们说，我们怀着喜悦和认真的态度来领导它。 他们说，相信我们。

人工智能是一个独特的营销挑战。 几年前，它被描述为无所不能——结束所有技术转变的技术转变。 ChatGPT 推出四个月后，Sam Altman 表示，这“甚至比一场技术革命还要大”。 Dario Amodei 将法学硕士比作“数据中心天才的国家”。

然后是生产力浪潮，向工人承诺这将使他们的工作变得更加轻松。 如果你相信埃隆·马斯克，你可能根本不需要工作。 然后总是有中国，实验室可以引用迫在眉睫的威胁来证明他们的惊人速度是合理的。

对中国的警告不会很快消失。 尽管元广告令人眼花缭乱，肖恩·斯派塞却发出了严厉的警告。 “美国不能在人工智能竞赛中输给中国，”这位前白宫新闻秘书、曾经的《与星共舞》参赛者在广告推文中写道。 我给斯派塞发了一封电子邮件，询问他对这则广告的看法，以及他认为这则广告表达了哪些公众舆论。 他忽略了这个问题。 “在主导人工智能的竞赛中没有第二名，”他写道。

这就是人工智能竞赛长期以来的主题：统治。 这些实验室试图在定价、人才、播客线路的微妙挖掘方面占据主导地位。 他们能否软化自己的形象以重新获得信任？

Anthropic 尝试了两周前在世界杯期间首次推出的自家广告。 它展示了一些可怕的图像——面部识别跟踪、墓地，是的，还有一座燃烧的房子——同时提出了一些可怕的问题。 “人工智能可以信任吗？” 画外音问道。 “如果需要的话，谁来踩刹车？” 答案是：人为的！ 我们在这里为您服务。

如果说这些广告证明了什么的话，那就是人工智能实验室意识到了人们的担忧有多么严重。

该广告遭到广泛批评。 安德森·霍洛维茨 (Andreessen Horowitz) 合伙人奥利维亚·摩尔 (Olivia Moore) 想知道 Anthropic 是否“积极试图流失用户”。 萨姆·奥尔特曼写道，他认为这是讽刺。 然而，它的结构在某种程度上与元广告非常相似：提出批评，然后将其关闭。

Anthropic 轻拍了批评者的头。 广告中的一个声音说道：“如果我们都能发出自己的声音，那么我觉得会更好。”这意味着公众对 Anthropic 的发展有发言权。 他们不知道；它甚至还不是一家上市公司。 该初创公司传达的信息是“难题中蕴藏着希望”，但并未提供任何回答这些问题的计划。

另一方面，Meta 则为批评者提供了机会。 “有些人会让你相信人工智能会让我们的联系减少，”广告的旁白说道。 “你相信吗”——这是什么，催眠？ 当然，梅塔是对抗这些无面耍蛇者的救世主。 他们是乐观主义者，是人工智能种族中的闪亮骑士。

不仅仅是LLM巨头。 Notion 在其最新的活动中回应了批评：“人工智能恐惧”广告牌。 这家软件公司为那些“担心人工智能会取代我们的工作”的来电者设立了热线。

信任很难获得。 目前尚不清楚这两种策略——拍头还是反驳——能否让人工智能的批评者得到安宁。

一些评论者喜欢元广告，称其解决了日益增长的厄运论。 其他人则称其“令人厌恶”和“令人难以置信的脱离现实”。 许多人嘲笑配乐的选择：大卫·鲍伊的《五年》，一首关于地球灭亡的歌曲。

宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院营销学教授戴维·鲁宾斯坦 (David Reibstein) 表示，人工智能实验室必须应对日益增长的批评。 他说，Anthropic 的广告“很大胆”，而 Meta 的广告却没有给他带来什么启发。 他说，传达的信息是“相信我们，因为我们是 Facebook”。 对于有人批评 Anthropic 提出了潜在危害，认为该公司本身正在怂恿这些潜在危害，他说：“我不认为这是虚伪的。 我认为这是敏感的。”

当联系到 Meta 的一位代表寻求置评时，他发送了一些广告高管的联系信息，并称该公司与该公司没有任何财务关系。 其中之一是创意机构 Portal A 的总裁扎克·布鲁姆 (Zach Blume)，他说他发现这两个广告“有力且有说服力”。

我还询问了 Joonas Virtanen，他是迷你应用初创公司 Wabi 的创始设计师，曾帮助 Airbnb 的聊天机器人变得“更有趣”，他对这些活动有何看法。 他表示，他更有可能相信 Anthropic 的做法，称其为“诚实”的广告，“像对待成年人一样对待人们”。 至于梅塔，他把甜甜的糖吐了出来。 “这有点公司的废话，”他说。 “它正在推销那种美好的愿景。”

Virtanen 从事科技工作；他很容易受益于人工智能的好处。 这些公司需要引进泡沫之外的人，那些宁愿住在核反应堆附近而不是数据中心的人。 他们会更难被说服。

当然，阿莫迪已经减弱了对即将到来的人工智能灾难的警告。 当然，奥特曼表示，他很高兴在人工智能破坏工作岗位的问题上“犯了错误”。 但种子已经种下了。 如果说这些广告证明了什么的话，那就是人工智能实验室意识到了人们的担忧有多么严重。 他们需要的不仅仅是彩虹和“难题”来根除它。
